question.text: On June 15, 1813, Bol´ıvar issued a Decree proclaiming this violent end against the Spanish in South America. This decree guaranteed no harm would come to anyone who murdered a Spaniard or had previously done so.
question.answerHtml: Decree of War to the Death (accept Decreto de Guerra a Muerte)
question.answer: Decree of War to the Death
question.clue: During the Admirable Campaign, Bolivar issued this Decree as a response to Spanish massacres. This order permitted murder of Spanish born citizens opposing independence.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people in the "Leaders" section of the 2017 TIME 100.
swap.text: This man won the 2016 Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to make peace with rebel groups in Colombia, including FARC.

question.leadin: In a 19th century civil war in this country, Fructuoso Rivera's Colorados fought Manuel Oribe's agrarian Blancos.
question.text: Name this South American country where wealthy businessmen in Montevideo [mon-tay-vih-DAY-oh] supported the Colorados, the eventual winning side.
question.clue: Raul Sendic led communist revolutionaries known as the Tupamaros in this country; this country's former president Jose Mujica used to be a Tupamaro.

swap.leadin: Smaller islands off the coast of this island include Gonˆave [go-nahv] Island near Port-au-Prince and Tortuga off the northern coast.
swap.text: Name this island whose land is divided between two modern countries.
swap.clue: After independence, this location was home to a separatist movement called La Trinitaria, which was led by Juan Pablo Duarte.

question.leadin: Answer the following about international relations in the Caribbean.
question.text: The US invaded this island nation in 1983 in which US intelligence agencies lied about mass graves caused by communist brutality to drum up support. Cuba sent aid for this nation, such as teachers, to its capital of St. George's.
question.clue: Prime Minister Eric Gairy, who had led the country from its 1974 independence from Britain, was ousted by Maurice Bishop in this country, the leader of the New Jewel Movement.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Mexican Constitution of 1857.
swap.text: Part of the Constitution of 1857 was drafted by this man, the first Zapotec President of Mexico. This man defeated Emperor Maximilian during the Second French Intervention.
swap.clue: Porforio Diaz helped this man win the Battle of Puebla, and later succeeded him as president.

question.leadin: A group of women who fought against this dictator used the underground name Las Mariposas and became a symbol of feminist resistance.
question.text: Name this dictator, nicknamed El Jefe, who was responsible for the Parsley Massacre. His order to assassinate those aforementioned women is believed to have led to his own assasination 6 months later in 1961.
question.clue: The novel Feast of the Goat by Mario Vargas Llosa describes the end of this man's reign, as well as his abuse of the wives of his advisors, and after his assassination Joaquin Balaguer was placed in power.

swap.text: Louverture ("LOO-ver-tchure") had earlier fought the mulatto Andre Rigaud ("rih-GO")for control over the Haitian Revolution in this war. This war is sometimes known as the "War of the South."
swap.clue: During the revolution, Toussaint Louverture fought the mulatto Andre Rigaud in this war. This war was pivotal for Louverture's control of southern Haiti.

question.leadin: On this holiday in 1647, people in Canterbury rioted on news that it was to be treated as any other working day with no sermon given.
question.text: Identify this holiday whose celebration was banned by Parliament in the mid-1640s.
question.clue: This date that alternately names the Baptist War led by deacon Samuel Sharpe in Jamaica.

swap.text: When King Joao wanted to return this possession back, his son Pedro refused, and with the help of the British in 1822 was able to secure this nation's independence. For 15 points-name this country that was discovered in 1500 by Portuguese admiral Pedro Alvares Cabral.
swap.clue: After "I Stay Day,"thiscountry's independence was declared with the slogan "Independence or Death," which became known as the Cry ofIpiranga.

question.leadin: He signed the the Treaty of Peace and Friendship with in 1984.
question.text: Name this guy who is arrested every few months by one government or another for his complicity in torture and assassinations as dictator of from 1973 to 1990.
question.answer: General Augusto Jose Ramon Pinochet Ugarte
question.clue: Patricio Aylwin succeeded this man as president of his country.

swap.text: This Cuban dictator deposed Gerardo Machado in 1933 but was overthrown himself in 1959 as Che Guevara and Fidel Castro headed the 26th of July Movement.
swap.clue: This leader of the United Action coalition stepped down from office after the withdrawal of American support for his regime, having faced an attack on the Moncada Barracks.

question.leadin: In order to stave off capture, this man hid in a Vatican embassy while American troops blasted rock music at the building.
question.text: Identify this Latin American dictator and former CIA informant who in 2007 was extradited to France after being overthrown by the US in Operation Just Cause back in 1989.
question.clue: He was simultaneously a paid informant for the CIA and the chief of military intelligence appointed by Omar Torrijos, and spied for Castro's Cuba.

swap.leadin: These settlements were heralded by Voltaire as "the triumph of humanity" after Antonio Ruiz de Montoya popularized them in Europe in The Spiritual Conquest of Paraguay.
swap.text: Give this name for South American Jesuit missions that protected over one hundred thousand native Guarani from Portuguese bandeirantes, but forced them to give up most tribal traditions.
swap.clue: What places primarily in modern-day Paraguay were home to many Tupi and Chiquito people in the 17th and 18th centuries? They resisted slave raiders and enjoyed economic success before dying out in the 1760s.

question.text: The Zimmerman Telegram sought a German alliance with this Mexican President, who drafted the Plan of Guadalupe, broke with Zapata and Pancho Villa after Aguascalientes, and was targeted by Obregon's Plan of Agua Prieta.
question.clue: As a result, ´Alvaro Obreg´on's supporters plotted the Plan of Agua Prieta to end this man's rule, and he was killed in May 1920.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Mexican feminism in the 20th century.
swap.text: In 1934, the feminist Maria del Refugio Garcia went on an 11-day hunger strike outside this Mexican President's home, after which he passed Article 34. This leader nationalized Mexican oil under Pemex and distributed land to farms called ejidos.
swap.clue: This politician cited Article 27 of his country's constitution in violating an agreement his predecessor made with Dwight Morrow.

question.text: This man served as the only vice president of Great Colombia, since Bolivar abolished the vice presidency in 1828 after coming to dislike him. In 1832, he became president of New Granada.
question.clue: Saenz was the target of rumors that she participated in General Jose Sarda's conspiracy against this leader. This leader defeated Antonio Narino in a Vice Presidency election after the passing of the Constitution of Cucuta.

swap.text: Before returning to power in 2007, Ortega was unseated in the 1990 election by a politician and former ally of this surname. The murder of a La Prensa editor with this surname was a major spark of the Sandinista revolution.
swap.clue: Pedro Joaquin of this family was an ardent anti-Somoza partisan who was assassinated in the early '80s. Pedro's wife Violeta defeated Daniel Ortega to became the President of Nicaragua in 1990.

question.text: The brouhaha erupted when a Paraguayan gunboat opened fire on this U.S. ship captained by Thomas Page, which was on a scientific expedition in the area, resulting in the death of an American seaman.

swap.text: The coup against Brazilian president Washington Luis was led by this corporatist leader of the Liberal Alliance, who modeled his ensuing rule of Brazil on Antonio Salazar's Estado Novo.
swap.clue: This nationalist and populist who presided over the Estado Novo in Brazil.
